detail.title: Operational Criteria for Objective Records
detail.summary: Objective records arise when an environment redundantly encodes and broadcasts pointer states of a system (Quantum Darwinism), providing multiple observers access to the same information. Crucially, environmental redundancy alone is insufficient; effective accessibility is gated by observer-dependent thresholds.
detail.reason: Synthesizing evidence regarding objectivity and redundancy.

detail.title: Information Scrambling and Record Accessibility
detail.summary: Quantum scrambling delocalizes information, complicating local retrieval. However, effective records remain accessible if the scrambling process respects specific pointer states that remain detectable despite global delocalization.

detail.title: Operational Criteria for Objective Records
detail.summary: Objective physical records are established when system pointer states are redundantly encoded into the environment via decoherence and Quantum Darwinism, allowing independent observers to access consistent information without disturbing the source system.
detail.reason: Revising the objective records notebook with newly retrieved peer evidence to strengthen the operational criteria for objective physical records.
